records.quote: The wax candle test successfully ignited in an opposed flow (akin to holding a candle upside down) and burned at five different flow velocities corresponding to the test matrix potentiometer settings as shown in Figure 3.1.
records.derivation: Ferkul chapter 3.1.1. The only candle in the Ferkul series is F4 ('Japan Wax candle' in Table A.2 page=113 and in the PSI table). Figure 3.1 caption, same page: 'Candle wick burning with opposed flow (upward flow).' Table A.2 says 'Stagnation' for F4 (R406). SHARED_LINEAGE: the same chapter says the candle was an unused BASS–I sample: 'A secondary objective was to burn any unused Burning and Suppression Solids—I (BASS–I) samples, of which there was a single wax candle.'

Conflicts with the series-level ReadMe paragraph=9 ('igniting the downstream end for an opposed flow flame spread geometry', held as R8), hence DISCREPANCY; the table is the per-test source.

records.quote: P19 194m 6.35-mm black rod –36 2 Concurrent

records.quote: A total of 20 PMMA flat samples were burnt during the BASS–II experimentation (Table 5.1). The sample thickness varied from 1 to 5 mm thick. The samples burnt were all either 1 or 2 cm wide. All the burns are either one sided or two sided. The airflow was always opposed.
records.derivation: Miller and Wichman chapter 5.3. Test ids: the Table 5.1 it points to ('TWENTY BURNING AND SUPPRESSION OF SOLIDS—II (BASS–II) TESTS', page=65) lists exactly M1 to M20. Proposed as a better-scoped replacement for R9 (pre-flight SRD matrix, not mapped to flown test numbers). Same chapter, page=63: 'The experiment took place in opposed flow with a varying O2 concentration (uncontrolled) and varying flow velocities (controlled).'
Table A.4 'MILLER TEST MATRIX', corroborates R410 per test. Column headed 'Sample distance' in the text layer (see R403).

records.quote: Sandra Olson burned three sizes of pmma rods (mostly clear), igniting the upstream end for a stagnation flame / concurrent flow geometry.
records.derivation: Same sentence as the held R7, re-proposed with the exact Olson test ids from the PSI table (PI column 'Olson'), because the build code cannot expand 'O1..' with a/b suffixes. This is the sentence that equates the stagnation flame with the concurrent flow geometry for the Olson rods (used by R417 and R418).

records.quote: For the first time, a series of concurrent rod flammability tests were conducted in microgravity aboard the International Space Station.
records.derivation: Abstract of chapter 6.0 'Individual Principal Investigator Report: Olson' (6.1 'Microgravity Flammability Boundary for Polymethylmethacrylate Rods in Axial Stagnation Flow'). The chapter says its tests are BASS–II (page=74: 'The BASS–II hardware used for these tests has been described in detail in Reference 14.') but does not list test numbers; ids are the PSI-table Olson series. Same chapter, page=74: 'Concurrent-flow flame spread tests burned an axisymmetric cylindrical PMMA rod having low heat losses to the downstream sample support pin.'

records.quote: TABLE 7.1.—TEST SUMMARY OF FLAT SIBALa FABRICS IN CONCURRENT FLOW IN BURNING AND SUPPRSSION SOLIDS (BASS AND BASS–II)
records.derivation: T'ien chapter 7.1, page=103: 'A total of 27 tests were carried out for the fabric samples in BASS–II, including six quenching tests, three nonignited tests, and one blowoff test. These are listed in Table 7.1.' The table rows carry ids as 'GMT45-T1', 'GMT175-T10', 'GMT178-T11', 'GMT216-T28a', etc.; the 27 BASS-II rows are the ids listed here. Excluded: the four rows the table marks 'BASS' (GMT96-T8, GMT96-T7, GMT131-T10, GMT222-T11), which are BASS (PSI-26) tests whose labels collide with BASS-II T7, T10, T11. BASS-II T10 and T11 are the GMT175 and GMT178 rows (dates match the PSI table). T3 and T7 (spherical section) are not in Table 7.1 (see R423).
